acceptance_status: Automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: Rust PreferencesForm owns opaque-profile draft binding, dirty-key state, refresh replacement decisions, text-save UI admission and site-rule pagination. Actual UTF-16 text already lives in the shared Rust editor. Native stores and validation remain authoritative.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

additional_performance_scenario_coverage.purpose: Execute all four opt-in performance scenarios as additional automated coverage, with their default 30 trials. Metal validation is enabled; these are not controlled CPU/GPU/drawable presentation comparisons.

contracts: Only an opaque profile ID and UI key/flags cross the controller ABI; Rust acquires no profile object, service handle or store mutation authority. Native profile/stale-action/managed-setting checks and data validation remain in force.

Unmanaged present fields refresh only when neither dirty nor composing. Managed values or a changed profile may replace a draft/preedit. Missing values disable the adapter but retain text and dirty state. Successful saves release only the saved key; failed saves retain it.

A profile transition clears all dirty keys and resets rule pagination to 50. Same-profile refresh retains dirty keys and the current page limit. Detach clears the profile binding and dirty state while category selection survives; actual native detach/reattach acceptance remains open.

Rust owns the 50-row pagination limit and resets on committed search edits and profile changes. More advances by 50 with saturation. Native normalized matching, rule display/callbacks, deferred mutation and profile guards remain unchanged.

A new shared backend test exercises two independent dirty fields, failed font/language saves, successful normalization, external pref changes, active IME refresh and switching away/back without writing drafts into another profile. Existing pagination, deferred profile-bound removal, managed store checks and disabled/IME admission tests remain in the gate.
The Views branch retains native dirty/profile/pagination state and the same refresh/save policy. No new crate/library/dependency or license is introduced.
limits: Preference UI copy/descriptions, remaining busy/status/form coordination, tools/provider pickers, other forms and browser-service panels, outer layout and native interaction/container ownership still require migration.
Manual IME/candidate-window, VoiceOver, complex bidi/RTL, pointer/trackpad, scale/theme, detach/reattach and GPU recovery acceptance remain open.
Optional scenarios provide execution coverage; no controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation speedup comparison is claimed.
Normal installed applications/profiles were untouched; no release bundle was packaged/signed. Final shipped-binary Apache-2.0/upstream license/notice acceptance remains open.

input.note: First Metal test injected text into invisible editors, which reject editing through Available()/Editable(). Native baseline accepted this synthetic call. Test now reveals each field through the actual search UI and verifies visibility before insertion; draft/save/profile assertions retained.

initial_test_probe.resolution: The initial new test injected text into invisible fields. Existing Rust editor admission rejects hidden-field edits; the Views baseline accepted this synthetic call. The test now reveals each field using the real search UI, asserts visibility and requests focus before input. Draft/save/profile assertions are retained; the initial failed run is retained.
